A 16-year-old previously healthy Chinese girl presented to emergency department with acute impaired consciousness, urinary incontinence, bilateral lower limb stiffness, and 1-week history of low-grade fever.
No relapse was observed in the first 3 years of follow-up.

extractions.value: Initial presentation mimicked fulminant septic shock with myocarditis, rhabdomyolysis, DIC, and multi-organ dysfunction. EEG showed generalized delta brush waves. Anti-Ro antibody positive. ANA 1:160. Voiding cystourethrogram showed neurogenic bladder. X-ray showed thoracolumbar scoliosis. Repeated anti-GAD level after treatment was 8 IU/mL.
extractions.quote: Initial investigation showed raised creatine kinase (108,510 IU/L) and troponin I (88,874 ng/L), deranged renal function, metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, and disseminated intravascular coagulation ... EEG revealed generalized delta brush waves ... positive anti-Ro antibody ... high antinuclear antibody (1:160) ... Voiding cystourethrogram showed features of neurogenic bladder ... X-ray showing thoracolumbar scoliosis ... anti-GAD level (8 IU/mL) also returned normal.
